import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 184

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/184](https://www.erdosproblems.com/184)
- [BM22] Bucić, M. and Montgomery, R., Towards the Erdős-Gallai Cycle Decomposition Conjecture.
  arXiv:2211.07689 (2022).
- [CFS14] Conlon, David and Fox, Jacob and Sudakov, Benny, Cycle packing. Random Structures
  Algorithms (2014), 608-626.
- [EGP66] Erdős, Paul and Goodman, A. W. and Pósa, Lajos, The representation of a graph by set
  intersections. Canadian J. Math. (1966), 106-112.
- [Er71] Erdős, P., Some unsolved problems in graph theory and combinatorial analysis. Combinatorial
  Mathematics and its Applications (Proc. Conf., Oxford, 1969) (1971), 97-109.
-/

open Filter SimpleGraph

namespace Erdos184

/--
A graph $H$ is a cycle or an edge if it is connected and 2-regular, or if it has exactly one edge.
-/
def IsCycleOrEdge {U : Type*} [Fintype U] (H : SimpleGraph U) : Prop :=
  open scoped Classical in
  (H.Connected ∧ H.IsRegularOfDegree 2) ∨ H.edgeFinset.card = 1

/-- D is a decomposition of G into subgraphs. -/
def IsDecomposition {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (D : Finset G.Subgraph) : Prop :=
  Set.PairwiseDisjoint (D : Set G.Subgraph) (fun H ↦ H.edgeSet) ∧
  (⋃ H ∈ D, H.edgeSet) = G.edgeSet

open scoped Classical in
/--
Any graph on $n$ vertices can be decomposed into $O(n)$ many edge-disjoint cycles and edges.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_184 :
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ,
      (f =O[atTop] fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ)) ∧
      ∀ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      ∃ (D : Finset G.Subgraph),
        (∀ H ∈ D, IsCycleOrEdge H.coe) ∧
        IsDecomposition G D ∧
        (D.card : ℝ) ≤ f (Fintype.card V) := by
  sorry

open scoped Classical in
/--
Erdős and Gallai [EGP66] proved that $O(n \log n)$ many cycles and edges suffices.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_184.variants.n_log_n :
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ,
      (f =O[atTop] fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) * Real.log (n : ℝ)) ∧
      ∀ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      ∃ (D : Finset G.Subgraph),
        (∀ H ∈ D, IsCycleOrEdge H.coe) ∧
        IsDecomposition G D ∧
        (D.card : ℝ) ≤ f (Fintype.card V) := by
  sorry

open scoped Classical in
/--
The graph $K_{3,n-3}$ shows that at least $(1+c)n$ many cycles and edges are required, for some
constant $c>0$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_184.variants.lower_bound :
    ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
      let G : SimpleGraph (Fin n) := fromRel (fun (i j : Fin n) => (i : ℕ) < 3 ∧ 3 ≤ (j : ℕ));
      ∀ (D : Finset G.Subgraph),
        (∀ H ∈ D, IsCycleOrEdge H.coe) →
        IsDecomposition G D →
        (1 + c) * (n : ℝ) ≤ (D.card : ℝ) := by
  sorry

open scoped Classical in
/--
In [Er71] Erdős suggests that only $n-1$ many cycles and edges are required if we do not
require them to be edge-disjoint.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_184.variants.covering :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∀ {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] [Nonempty V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      ∃ (D : Finset G.Subgraph),
        (∀ H ∈ D, IsCycleOrEdge H.coe) ∧
        (⋃ H ∈ D, H.edgeSet) = G.edgeSet ∧
        (D.card : ℝ) ≤ (Fintype.card V : ℝ) - 1 := by
  sorry

open scoped Classical in
/--
The best bound available is due to Bucić and Montgomery [BM22], who prove that $O(n\log^* n)$ many
cycles and edges suffice, where $\log^*$ is the iterated logarithm function.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_184.variants.bucic_montgomery :
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ,
      (f =O[atTop] fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) * (Real.iteratedLog (n : ℝ) : ℝ)) ∧
      ∀ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      ∃ (D : Finset G.Subgraph),
        (∀ H ∈ D, IsCycleOrEdge H.coe) ∧
        IsDecomposition G D ∧
        (D.card : ℝ) ≤ f (Fintype.card V) := by
  sorry

open scoped Classical in
/--
Conlon, Fox, and Sudakov [CFS14] proved that $O_\epsilon(n)$ cycles and edges suffice if $G$ has
minimum degree at least $\epsilon n$, for any $\epsilon>0$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_184.variants.conlon_fox_sudakov :
    ∀ ε > 0, ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ,
      (f =O[atTop] fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ)) ∧
      ∀ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      (G.minDegree : ℝ) ≥ ε * (Fintype.card V : ℝ) →
      ∃ (D : Finset G.Subgraph),
        (∀ H ∈ D, IsCycleOrEdge H.coe) ∧
        IsDecomposition G D ∧
        (D.card : ℝ) ≤ f (Fintype.card V) := by
  sorry

end Erdos184

status_issues.source_status: Solved positively by L. Pyber in 1985: An Erdős–Gallai conjecture, Combinatorica 5(1), 67–79.
status_issues.evidence: BM22’s Introduction, under “Covering problems,” states: “In 1985, Pyber ... proved the covering version ... showing that the edges of any n-vertex graph can be covered with n-1 cycles and edges.” https://arxiv.org/e-print/2211.07689. CFS14’s Introduction independently records the same result: https://arxiv.org/e-print/1310.0632.
status_issues.suggested_change: Change the category to research solved and replace answer(sorry) with answer(True). Update the docstring/reference to mention Pyber’s proof.

reformulations.difference: Lean chooses a real-valued function f = O(n) that bounds a suitable decomposition for every finite graph, rather than stating a uniform Cn bound directly.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A big-O estimate gives f(n) ≤ cn for all sufficiently large n. Enlarge the constant to absorb the finitely many exceptional positive n. At n = 0 the graph has no edges and admits the empty decomposition. Conversely, a uniform Cn bound supplies f(n) = Cn. This equivalence was proved for arbitrary vertex universes as Review184.functional_iff_constant in /workspace/review/equivalences.lean, without using any sorry-backed theorem.

reformulations.difference: Real.iteratedLog counts iterations of the natural logarithm, whereas BM22 §2.1 specifies base-two logarithms.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Let L_e and L_2 denote the respective first-hit counts at threshold 1. Their inverse thresholds are towers E_0 = T_0 = 1, E_(k+1) = exp(E_k), and T_(k+1) = 2^(T_k). These satisfy T_k ≤ E_k ≤ T_(k+2); the upper estimate follows inductively from E_k ≤ T_(k+2)/2. Consequently L_e(n) ≤ L_2(n) ≤ L_e(n) + 2. For n ≥ 2 this gives n L_e(n) ≤ n L_2(n) ≤ 3 n L_e(n), so the big-O claims are equivalent. Termination of natural-log iteration was proved separately in Lean, ruling out the empty-set default in its sInf definition; the full base-change equivalence was not formalized.

review.notes: Checked both definitions and all six theorem statements. Finite connected 2-regular graphs give precisely simple cycles. Allowing isolated vertices in a one-edge piece does not change any assertion: they can be deleted without changing its edge set or the number of pieces. Independent Lean checks in /workspace/review/ verified the edge-partition definition against unique edge membership, the K_{3,n-3} construction, empty and smallest graph cases, minimum-degree boundaries, and termination of logarithm iteration. The lower-bound quantifiers agree with the parity/cycle-length bound 4(n-3)/3, which yields, for example, c = 1/4 for n ≥ 48. No repository files were edited.
